mistakes.name: Ball too far from feet
mistakes.plain_english: The ball is too far in front of you while running with it. Any defender can easily intercept it.
mistakes.root_cause: Pushing the ball too hard per touch, or running faster than your ball control allows.
mistakes.correction: Take smaller, more controlled touches. Keep the ball within one touch range at all times.

mistakes.name: Head down while dribbling
mistakes.plain_english: You are watching the ball while dribbling instead of looking up to read the game. You can't see defenders coming.
mistakes.root_cause: Insufficient touch-feel — not confident enough to dribble without watching the ball.
mistakes.correction: Practise dribbling to a cone while focusing your eyes on a fixed point ahead. Force yourself to feel the ball.

mistakes.name: Always going the same direction
mistakes.plain_english: You always cut to your stronger foot. Defenders know what you will do before you do it.
mistakes.root_cause: Over-reliance on dominant foot creates a pattern defenders can read.
mistakes.correction: Practise moves in both directions equally. In training, force yourself to go left when your instinct says right.

mistakes.name: Dribbling without feinting
mistakes.plain_english: You run directly at defenders without body feints. They can easily time their tackle.
mistakes.root_cause: Not practising deceptive movements — body feints, shoulder drops, or step-overs.
mistakes.correction: Before accelerating past a defender, use one feint to shift their weight. Then go.

mistakes.name: Slow acceleration after touch
mistakes.plain_english: After a good touch, you don't accelerate quickly enough to beat the defender.
mistakes.root_cause: Lack of explosive first step — waiting too long after the touch to accelerate.
mistakes.correction: The touch and the sprint must happen in one motion. Push the ball with your touch and go immediately.
